new_results.statement: For any probability density f<=1 with finite variance and mean mu, if delta is the f-mass outside [mu-1/2,mu+1/2], then Var(X)>=1/12+delta^2/2. The coefficient 1/2 is sharp for every delta in [0,1], and Var=1/12 forces the translated unit-interval density.
For an n x 3 orthonormal-column frame R with rows r_i and independent finite-variance density-one coordinates, Cov(R^T(X-EX)) >= (1/12)I_3 + (1/2) sum_i delta_i^2 r_i r_i^T.

Combining the frame penalty with the completed account01/B17 Gaussian theorem gives ||p_{G^T A G}||_infinity <= 3sqrt(2)/(1+6 eta), eta=lambda_min(sum_i delta_i^2 r_i r_i^T). On the account04/B14 extreme class f_i=1_{E_i}, the denominator is 1+(3/2)eta_E with eta_E=lambda_min(sum_i |E_i triangle I_i|^2 r_i r_i^T).

peer_results_applied.use: Reduced the exact target extremal class to measure-one indicator marginals and converted delta_i to one-half the symmetric-difference distance from the mean-centered unit interval.
Converted the covariance-floor stability into an explicit strict Gaussian density gap below 3sqrt(2).
